## Findings (SPEC)

**1. Fix is incomplete when `baseURL` is configured — `buildFullPath` runs before `buildURL`.**
Location: added lines in `lib/helpers/buildURL.js`; request path `lib/helpers/resolveConfig.js:57-61`, `lib/core/Axios.js:243-250`.
Requirement: the issue objective — `axios.get(new URL(...), {params})` should work; the PR says it "convert[s] URL objects to strings before processing."
Mechanism: `resolveConfig` calls `buildURL(buildFullPath(baseURL, url, allowAbsoluteUrls), ...)`. `isAbsoluteURL` returns `false` for non-strings (`lib/helpers/isAbsoluteURL.js:14-16`), so a `URL` object is classified relative; if `baseURL` is set, `combineURLs` executes `relativeURL.replace(/^\/+/, '')` (`lib/helpers/combineURLs.js:13`), and `URL` has no `replace` → TypeError. Even without a throw, an absolute `URL` would be wrongly prefixed by `baseURL`.
Impact: `axios.get(new URL(...))` still fails whenever a `baseURL` is set; only the no-baseURL reproduction is fixed. Normalizing the URL before `buildFullPath` would be required.
Status: conditional (requires a configured `baseURL`).

**2. Added "without params" test appears inconsistent with the insertion point.**
Location: `lib/helpers/buildURL.js` added lines, inserted immediately after a block ending `return url; }` (diff context); test in `tests/unit/helpers/buildURL.test.js`.
Requirement: PR claim "should support URL object without params."
Mechanism: the conversion sits after an early `return url;` guard. If that guard is the falsy-`params` return (consistent with the test name), `buildURL(url, null)` returns the `URL` object, so `expect(buildURL(url, null)).toEqual(url.toString())` compares an object to a string and would not match.
Impact: the no-params path is not converted by the shown code, contradicting the claim.
Status: conditional/unverifiable — the guard condition itself is not shown in the material.

**3. Public typings still require `string`.**
Location: `index.d.ts:611-628` (unchanged).
Requirement: objective "support URL object as input."
Mechanism: overloads declare `url: string`; passing a `URL` object remains a TypeScript error.
Impact: TS consumers cannot use the new capability without a cast.
Status: demonstrated for the type surface (runtime behavior is separate).

No other material SPEC gaps are supported by the provided text.
